newsitem.title: USA: TI sees 1997 a year of transition.
newsitem.headline: TI sees 1997 a year of transition.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said it enters 1997 viewing the year as a period of transition that will see it tested by continued difficult market conditions even as it moves away from several large business lines.
The company enters 1997 having agreed to dispose of its defense and mobile computing businesses, the latter to Acer Inc in a sale pact announced today.
Late last year, TI agreed to sell its defense business to Raytheon Co.

In a statement announcing its fourth quarter results -- which included a net loss of $0.15 per share --TI said it has made progress in overcoming market difficulties but "we still have work to do and 1997 will be a year of transition."

Among the issues facing the company are low prices for memory chips. Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) prices remain volatile, TI said, and it expects the market for memory to remain difficult over the near term.
In the coming year, TI said it will cut capital expenditures at its continuing operations by nearly half, but research and development spending will increase slightly.
TI said it plans $1.1 billion in continuing operations capital expenditures in 1997, off from $2.1 billion in 1996.
R&D spending will rise to $1.1 billion from $1.0 billion.
